title: DIO/ODI Reference Model
description:
This record publishes the DIO/ODI Reference Model v0.5.0, a versioned machine-readable reference layer for Digital Identity Optimization (DIO) and the Ontology of Digital Identity (ODI). DIO is the applied discipline concerned with improving the conditions under which an entity's digital identity is reconstructed from its distributed digital representational state; ODI provides the theoretical meta-layer for examining the existence, persistence, variation, and reconstruction of that identity. The model is designed to make the DIO/ODI conceptual system consistently identifiable and interpretable across heterogeneous environments including artificial intelligence, search engines, knowledge graphs, and human observers.

The Reference Model operates above the distributed DIO/ODI publication corpus rather than replacing it. It consolidates and cross-references concepts developed across the canonical multilingual Manifest, the DIO Conceptual Framework, The Crisis of Entity Resolution in Heterogeneous AI Environments, Minimum Viable DIO (MVDIO), and the subsequent Taxonomic Note on Reconstruction Failure Modes. Each concept retains source provenance, and later refinement does not erase the historical role of earlier publications. The model therefore provides a stable semantic layer through which the corpus can be navigated as one evolving, versioned conceptual object.

At its core is the DIO/ODI Reference Vocabulary v0.2.0, published in SKOS/RDF and JSON-LD under stable concept URIs. It represents the principal analytical distinctions of MVDIO, including the semantic field, distributed representational state, observation domain, observer, reconstruction mechanism, the canonical plural concept Identity-Preserving Constraints, identity-preserving variation, referential continuity, and semantic coherence. The former singular vocabulary entry is retained separately with an editorial history note; no semantic relation between the singular and plural concepts is asserted. It also preserves the K6 Semantic Connectome as the complete ordered set of six mutually conditioned dimensions—Entity, Representation, Interpretation, Trust, Relationship, and Reconstruction. K6 is not represented as a sequential pipeline or as a literal causal graph.

The model also represents the current non-exclusive, multi-level hierarchy of Reconstruction Failure Modes: Referential Reconstruction Failures (Entity Substitution, Merge Failure, Split Failure, Entity Omission); Semantic Coherence Failures (Semantic Fragmentation); Temporal Reconstruction Failures (Temporal Discontinuity, Temporal Misalignment); and Contextual Adequacy Failures (Contextual Displacement). Identity Collapse remains a phenomenon-level concept outside this hierarchy. Semantic Vulnerability is represented as a robustness-related property rather than a realized failure mode, with Semantic Robustness as its conceptual counterpart; Reconstruction Capture remains a related concept without stronger causal commitment.

Derived Application Mappings are deliberately separated from the canonical vocabulary. The RAG mapping projects DIO Reconstruction Failure Modes onto generic retrieval-augmented generation pipeline loci, mechanisms, observable symptoms, and hypothetical incidents. The v0.4.0 snapshot also includes an analytical extension on iterative and hypothesis-conditioned evidence acquisition: it examines how a working hypothesis may shape successive query, tool, and source choices, the evidence exposed or selected, and later hypothesis updates. These process-level conditions are neither new canonical DIO/ODI concepts nor new failure modes; their relation to reconstruction outcomes remains conditional and non-deterministic. The HEM × DIO mapping uses the externally defined Heterogeneous Entity Matching taxonomy as an analytical axis for examining how heterogeneous input conditions may contribute to reconstruction failures or increase Semantic Vulnerability. The Commit-Boundary × Policy-as-Code mapping applies the DIO/ODI commit-boundary authorization obligations described in Beránek's 2026 paper, Constraining the Commit Boundary: A DIO/ODI-Informed Authorization Guardrail for Agentic Entity Resolution (https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.23580733), to policy-as-code controls, using OPA/Rego and Cedar as reference points. It distinguishes policy decisions, evidence validation, enforcement, version freshness, and atomic-write concerns while documenting integration gaps; it does not claim a complete or empirically validated implementation. These mappings are non-normative and non-deterministic: they apply DIO/ODI concepts to external domains without redefining either the canonical vocabulary or the external frameworks.

Version 0.5.0 preserves the operational corpus metadata registry introduced in the prior release for work identities, DOI/version information, typed inter-work relations, canonical references, distribution representations, and an ordered keyword grammar. The keyword grammar uses invariant and master-ordered semantic chunks so that recurring concepts retain stable lexical form and relative position across records. Together with persistent identifiers, explicit provenance, typed relations such as References, IsDerivedFrom and IsIdenticalTo, and verified distribution equivalence, this metadata layer applies a core DIO principle to DIO itself: the identity of the discipline and its works should be reconstructable from explicit, distributed, mutually reinforcing representations rather than inferred anew from isolated prose on every encounter.

The Reference Model is not a completed formal ontology and does not silently strengthen claims beyond the published corpus. Its current semantic layer is intentionally SKOS-first; stronger OWL axioms should be introduced only where source publications and subsequent review justify them. The archived release package is a versioned research software artifact and is not asserted to be identical to the persistent namespace itself. Version 0.5.0 incorporates Reference Vocabulary v0.2.0 and adds the separate canonical concept Identity-Preserving Constraints while retaining the former singular URI as a historical entry. Earlier references are not retroactively migrated, and no semantic relation between the two concepts is asserted. The archive carries forward the Commit-Boundary × Policy-as-Code mapping, the HEM × DIO mapping, and the iterative/hypothesis-conditioned RAG extension. The Reference Model remains SKOS-first and is not presented as a completed formal ontology. The extension is analytical and is not represented as empirically validated; the Reference Model is not a completed formal ontology.
